This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# Monolith

```
 _____    _____________   __________     ___________________    ___
|     \  /             \ |          |   |                   |  |   |
|      \/       __      \|    __    |   |    ___     ___    |__|   |
|              |  |          |  |   |   |   |   |   |   |          |
|   |\    /|   |__|          |__|   |___|   |   |   |   |    __    |
|   | \__/ |          |\                    |   |   |   |   |  |   |
|___|      |__________| \___________________|   |___|   |___|  |___|
```

A data hoarder's dream come true: bundle any web page into a single HTML file. You can finally replace that gazillion of open tabs with a gazillion of .html files stored somewhere on your precious little drive.

Unlike the conventional "Save page as", `monolith` not only saves the target document, it embeds CSS, image, and JavaScript assets **all at once**, producing a single HTML5 document that is a joy to store and share.

If compared to saving websites with `wget -mpk`, this tool embeds all assets as data URLs and therefore lets browsers render the saved page exactly the way it was on the Internet, even when no network connection is available.

## Usage

```console
monolith https://lyrics.github.io/db/P/Portishead/Dummy/Roads/ -o %title%.%timestamp%.html
```

```console
cat some-site-page.html | monolith -aIiFfcMv -b https://some.site/ - > some-site-page-with-assets.html
```

## Options

 - `-a`: Exclude audio sources
 - `-b`: Use `custom base URL`
 - `-B`: Forbid retrieving assets from specified domain(s)
 - `-c`: Exclude CSS
 - `-C`: Read cookies from `file`
 - `-d`: Allow retrieving assets only from specified `domain(s)`
 - `-e`: Ignore network errors
 - `-E`: Save document using `custom encoding`
 - `-f`: Omit frames
 - `-F`: Exclude web fonts
 - `-h`: Print help information
 - `-i`: Remove images
 - `-I`: Isolate the document
 - `-j`: Exclude JavaScript
 - `-k`: Accept invalid X.509 (TLS) certificates
 - `-m`: Output in MHTML format instead of HTML
 - `-M`: Don't add timestamp and URL information
 - `-n`: Extract contents of NOSCRIPT elements
 - `-o`: Write output to `file` (use "-" for STDOUT)
 - `-q`: Be quiet
 - `-t`: Adjust `network request timeout`
 - `-u`: Provide `custom User-Agent`
 - `-v`: Exclude videos
 - `-V`: Print version number

## Whitelisting and blacklisting domains

Options `-d` and `-B` provide control over what domains can be used to retrieve assets from, e.g.:

```console
monolith -I -d example.com -d www.example.com https://example.com -o example-only.html
```

```console
monolith -I -B -d .googleusercontent.com -d googleanalytics.com -d .google.com https://example.com -o example-no-ads.html
```

## Dynamic content

Monolith doesn't feature a JavaScript engine, hence websites that retrieve and display data after initial load may require usage of additional tools.

For example, Chromium (Chrome) can be used to act as a pre-processor for such pages:

```console
chromium --headless --window-size=1920,1080 --run-all-compositor-stages-before-draw --virtual-time-budget=9000 --incognito --dump-dom https://github.com | monolith - -I -b https://github.com -o github.html
```

## Authentication

```console
monolith https://username:password@example.com -o example-basic-auth.html
```

## Proxies

Please set `https_proxy`, `http_proxy`, and `no_proxy` environment variables.

messages.output: 0 # Monolith ``` _____ _____________ __________ ___________________ ___ | \ / \ | | | | | | | \/ __ \| __ | | ___ ___ |__| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |\ /| |__| |__| |___| | | | | __ | | | \__/ | |\ | | | | | | | |___| |__________| \___________________| |___| |___| |___| ``` A data hoarder's dream come true: bundle any web page into a single HTML file. You can finally replace that gazillion of open tabs with a gazillion of .html files stored somewhere on your precious little drive. Unlike the conventional "Save page as", `monolith` not only saves the target document, it embeds CSS, image, and JavaScript assets **all at once**, producing a single HTML5 document that is a joy to store and share. If compared to saving websites with `wget -mpk`, this tool embeds all assets as data URLs and therefore lets browsers render the saved page exactly the way it was on the Internet, even when no network connection is available. ## Usage ```console monolith https://lyrics.github.io/db/P/Portishead/Dummy/Roads/ -o %title%.%timestamp%.html ``` ```console cat some-site-page.html | monolith -aIiFfcMv -b https://some.site/ - > some-site-page-with-assets.html ``` ## Options - `-a`: Exclude audio sources - `-b`: Use `custom base URL` - `-B`: Forbid retrieving assets from specified domain(s) - `-c`: Exclude CSS - `-C`: Read cookies from `file` - `-d`: Allow retrieving assets only from specified `domain(s)` - `-e`: Ignore network errors - `-E`: Save document using `custom encoding` - `-f`: Omit frames - `-F`: Exclude web fonts - `-h`: Print help information - `-i`: Remove images - `-I`: Isolate the document - `-j`: Exclude JavaScript - `-k`: Accept invalid X.509 (TLS) certificates - `-m`: Output in MHTML format instead of HTML - `-M`: Don't add timestamp and URL information - `-n`: Extract contents of NOSCRIPT elements - `-o`: Write output to `file` (use "-" for STDOUT) - `-q`: Be quiet - `-t`: Adjust `network request timeout` - `-u`: Provide `custom User-Agent` - `-v`: Exclude videos - `-V`: Print version number ## Whitelisting and blacklisting domains Options `-d` and `-B` provide control over what domains can be used to retrieve assets from, e.g.: ```console monolith -I -d example.com -d www.example.com https://example.com -o example-only.html ``` ```console monolith -I -B -d .googleusercontent.com -d googleanalytics.com -d .google.com https://example.com -o example-no-ads.html ``` ## Dynamic content Monolith doesn't feature a JavaScript engine, hence websites that retrieve and display data after initial load may require usage of additional tools. For example, Chromium (Chrome) can be used to act as a pre-processor for such pages: ```console chromium --headless --window-size=1920,1080 --run-all-compositor-stages-before-draw --virtual-time-budget=9000 --incognito --dump-dom https://github.com | monolith - -I -b https://github.com -o github.html ``` ## Authentication ```console monolith https://username:password@example.com -o example-basic-auth.html ``` ## Proxies Please set `https_proxy`, `http_proxy`, and `no_proxy` environment variables. --- file:///tmp/full_elements.html file:///tmp/a.css (file not found) file:///tmp/exists.png file:///tmp/exists.png file:///tmp/exists.png file:///tmp/exists.png file:///tmp/exists.png file:///tmp/exists.png file:///tmp/vid.mp4 file:///tmp/exists.png file:///tmp/vid2.mp4 (file not found) file:///tmp/aud.mp3 file:///tmp/frame.html file:///tmp/app.js (file not found) file:///tmp/a.css (file not found) file:///tmp/exists.png hi hi hi hi file:///tmp/css_test.html file:///tmp/a.css file:///tmp/font.woff hi hi hi

# Monolith

```

|     \  /             \ |          |   |                   |  |   |

|   | \__/ |          |\                    |   |   |   |   |  |   |
|___|      |__________| \___________________|   |___|   |___|  |___|
```

A data hoarder's dream come true: bundle any web page into a single HTML file. You can finally replace that gazillion of open tabs with a gazillion of .html files stored somewhere on your precious little drive.

Unlike the conventional "Save page as", `monolith` not only saves the target document, it embeds CSS, image, and JavaScript assets **all at once**, producing a single HTML5 document that is a joy to store and share.

If compared to saving websites with `wget -mpk`, this tool embeds all assets as data URLs and therefore lets browsers render the saved page exactly the way it was on the Internet, even when no network connection is available.

## Usage

```console
monolith https://lyrics.github.io/db/P/Portishead/Dummy/Roads/ -o %title%.%timestamp%.html
```

```console
cat some-site-page.html | monolith -aIiFfcMv -b https://some.site/ - > some-site-page-with-assets.html
```

def main():
    opts = parse_args(sys.argv)
    # Validate encoding
    validate_encoding(opts.encoding)
    # Handle cookie file
    handle_cookie_file(opts.cookie_file)
    # Validate insecure etc.

    # Check output file preparation
    output_path = opts.output
    # If output is None, output to stdout
    # If output is "-", also stdout

    # Handle target retrieval
    is_stdin = (opts.target == "-")
    if is_stdin:
        html_bytes, doc_url, base_url, is_stdin_flag = get_target_content(opts.target, opts)
        # For stdin, doc_url is None, is_stdin True, base_url is opts.base_url
        # Read encoding? If opts.encoding provided, decode using that?
        # But get_target_content already read stdin as bytes
        # Need to handle decoding based on opts.encoding if provided
        # For file and http, we handled encoding later? We'll handle after.
        # For stdin, we need to handle charset meta? Not needed.
        # Determine html_text decoding
        # Use opts.encoding if provided, else utf-8
        encoding_to_use = opts.encoding or 'utf-8'
        # But stdin data may be bytes, decode
        # We'll handle later in parse
        html_bytes_for_parse = html_bytes
        base_for_parse = base_url
        doc_url_for_banner = None
    else:
        # Not stdin
        # Check if target is file or url via get_target_content
        html_bytes, doc_url, base_url, is_stdin_flag = get_target_content(opts.target, opts)
        # doc_url is final URL (file://... or http://...)
        # base_url is same as doc_url unless overridden by -b? But get_target_content returns base as doc_url, but parse will handle -b override separately
        # For file, doc_url is file:// path, base_url is file:// path
        html_bytes_for_parse = html_bytes
        base_for_parse = base_url
        doc_url_for_banner = doc_url
        # But if target was http and failed, get_target_content already exited
        # If target was file not found and not is_url, then get_target_content would have treated as URL and exited with error, but for file:// missing case, it also exited
        # So success here

    # Handle encoding enforcement: if opts.encoding provided, we need to ensure output has meta charset with that encoding
    # In earlier test, -E UTF-8 with file gave meta charset UTF-8, even if original was utf-8, they normalized to uppercase UTF-8
    # So we will handle after parsing.

    # Verbose output (unless quiet)
    if not opts.quiet:
        if not is_stdin:
            # Print doc_url or base?
            # For file, print file://... (doc_url)
            # For http, print http://...
            # But for our file case, doc_url is file://...
            # Need to print to stderr
            if doc_url_for_banner:
                eprint(doc_url_for_banner)
            # Also for each asset fetch, we already printed in fetch_asset

    # Parse HTML
    # Determine encoding for parsing: Use opts.encoding if provided else detect from meta charset or utf-8
    # Simplify: use opts.encoding or utf-8
    parse_enc = opts.encoding or 'utf-8'
    # But for file that is latin-1 encoded, without -E, parsing as utf-8 will replace invalid bytes with � (as observed earlier with enc_latin.html without -E)
    # So that's correct.

    root = parse_html(html_bytes_for_parse, encoding=parse_enc)

    # Process HTML with opts, base, doc_url, is_stdin
    # Need to pass effective base for resolving: base_for_parse may be overridden by -b, but process_html handles -b
    # So pass base_for_parse as document base, and let process_html handle -b override
    process_html(root, opts, base_for_parse, doc_url_for_banner, is_stdin)

    # Handle encoding meta after processing
    if opts.encoding:
        # Need to ensure head has meta charset with opts.encoding
        # Find head
        head_node = find_node(root, "head")
        if head_node:
            # Check if there's existing meta charset?
            # Look for meta with charset attribute or http-equiv content-type?
            found = False
            for n in list(traverse(root)):
                if n.tag == "meta":
                    # check charset attr
                    for k,v in n.attrs:
                        if k.lower() == "charset":
                            # Update to opts.encoding
                            # Preserve original case of attribute name? Keep as "charset"
                            # Update value to opts.encoding as provided? In earlier test, input UTF-8 vs utf-8 etc.
                            # For -E UTF-8, output was charset="UTF-8" (uppercase)
                            # For -E windows-1252, output was charset="windows-1252" (lower)
                            # So we should use opts.encoding as is, but maybe normalized?
                            # We'll use as provided
                            for idx, (kk,vv) in enumerate(n.attrs):
                                if kk.lower() == "charset":
                                    n.attrs[idx] = (kk, opts.encoding)
                            found = True
                            break
                    if found:
                        break
                    # Also check http-equiv content-type with charset
                    for k,v in n.attrs:
                        if k.lower() == "http-equiv" and v.lower() == "content-type":
                            # Look for content attr with charset
                            for kk,vv in n.attrs:
                                if kk.lower() == "content":
                                    # content like "text/html; charset=utf-8"
                                    # Update charset part
                                    # Simple: replace charset=...
                                    new_content = re.sub(r'charset\s*=\s*[^;\s]+', f'charset={opts.encoding}', vv, flags=re.I)
                                    if new_content == vv:
                                        new_content = vv + f"; charset={opts.encoding}"
                                    for idx2, (kk2,vv2) in enumerate(n.attrs):
                                        if kk2.lower() == "content":
                                            n.attrs[idx2] = (kk2, new_content)
                                    found = True
                                    break
                            break
                    if found:
                        break
            if not found:
                # Create new meta charset
                meta = Node(tag="meta", is_void=True)
                meta.is_added = True
                meta.attrs = [("charset", opts.encoding)]
                # Insert as first child of head? Usually charset is first. We'll insert at beginning?
                head_node.children.insert(0, meta)
                meta.parent = head_node
        # Also need to ensure that if head doesn't exist, we create?

    # Serialize HTML
    html_output = serialize_node(root, opts)

    # Add banner if not -M and not is_stdin? Actually banner for file and http, but not for stdin without -M? Let's check:
    # For stdin without -M, output had no banner. For stdin with -M, also no banner. For file with -M, no banner. For file without -M, banner present.
    # So banner only for non-stdin when -M not set.
    # For http, banner would be "Saved from http://..." else "Saved from local source"
    # For file, banner is "Saved from local source at <timestamp> using monolith vX"
    # For http, banner is "Saved from http://... at <timestamp> using monolith vX"
    # For mhtml, banner is inside the html part? Let's see: mhtml output had banner inside html part as comment before html.
    # So we need to generate banner comment.

    if not opts.no_metadata and not is_stdin:
        # Generate timestamp: ISO 8601 UTC with Z, like 2026-09-06T14:32:10Z
        timestamp = datetime.datetime.utcnow().strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
        if doc_url_for_banner and doc_url_for_banner.startswith("http"):
            banner = f"<!-- Saved from {doc_url_for_banner} at {timestamp} using monolith v2.11.0 -->\n"
        else:
            banner = f"<!-- Saved from local source at {timestamp} using monolith v2.11.0 -->\n"
        html_output = banner + html_output
    elif not opts.no_metadata and is_stdin:
        # For stdin with base_url, should banner be from that base URL? Let's see: In earlier test, stdin with -b http://example.com/ gave output without banner. So for stdin, no banner regardless?
        # Actually check: echo '<html>...' | ./executable - -b http://example.com/ gave output without banner (just html). So stdin never has banner, even with base.
        # So we do not add banner for stdin.
        pass

    # Handle mhtml if needed
    if opts.mhtml:
        # MHTML format: multipart/related with boundary
        # Observed output:
        # MIME-Version: 1.0\r\n
        # Content-Type: multipart/related; boundary="----=_NextPart_000_0000"\r\n
        # \r\n
        # ------=_NextPart_000_0000\r\n
        # Content-Type: text/html; charset="utf-8"\r\n
        # Content-Location: http://example.com/\r\n
        # \r\n
